name: Wales
summary:
Wales's devolved administration publicly maintains an LGBTQ+ Action Plan with a standing update page issued after the For Women Scotland judgment (19 December 2025), and has enacted statutory school guidance ("Rights, Respect, Equality," consultation May 2025) obliging schools to challenge bullying and harassment on gender-reassignment grounds with recording and monitoring, alongside a dedicated national guidance for supporting trans children in development through 2025–26. These measures represent an active state posture of inclusion at a time when the UK-wide EHRC single-sex-services code (in force 5 August 2026) creates a biological-sex facility-exclusion floor identical in Wales to England.

For a visitor the practical risk of service refusal is unchanged — the code binds Welsh facilities as equally as English ones — but the visible institutional commitment (Action Plan maintained, school recording obligations, FOI-disclosed guidance work) shapes policing culture and public discourse. Score sits +0.03 above the national anchor: Wales is not materially safer on facilities, but it is the only devolved administration actively counter-signalling the national climate with published protection programmes. Above England, which has no equivalent positive devolved signal.

name: Northern Ireland
summary:
Northern Ireland carries three sub-national negatives absent elsewhere in the UK: Education Minister Paul Givan ordered the 2019 transgender-pupils guidance withdrawn from the Education Authority website after the FWS ruling, calling it "unlawful and flawed"; the Justice Minister's attempt to include transgender people as a protected group in hate-crime sentencing reform was stalled (reported DUP obstruction); and the Rainbow Project records a pattern of paramilitary-flavoured anti-LGB&T violence including a pipe bomb thrown through the home of a trans woman in Derry/Londonderry described by PSNI as a "sectarian hate crime," a 2019 Belfast city-centre assault hospitalising a gay man, and an average of ~290 anti-LGB&T incidents per year (2013–2017) with rising transgender-identity strand counts to September 2025.

Counter-balancing: PSNI/NISRA track a separate "transgender identity" category (unlike England and Wales), evidencing institutional recognition; the Health Minister publicly defended gender-identity service funding (£800k+ uplift) against DUP/TUV criticism, showing the executive is split rather than uniformly hostile. No criminal ban on expression or police-enforced facility prohibition exists — the risk mechanism mirrors the national EHRC code (service refusal by staff) plus street-level violence.

Score −0.06 below the national anchor: active state removal of protections (guidance withdrawal, legislative exclusion from sentencing enhancement) compounds a patterned violence record in a paramilitary context. Materially worse than Wales (0.51), which maintains published inclusion programmes, and worse than England where the absence of a devolved positive signal is offset by the absence of a devolved negative one.
